questions.question: Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, born on this day in 1935, is a first cousin of which monarch?
questions.explanation: His father was a brother of George VI and Edward VIII, which makes him a first cousin of the late Queen Elizabeth II.
questions.context:
On this day in 1935: Prince Edward, Duke of Kent
Prince Edward, Duke of Kent (British prince (born 1935)): Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, is a member of the British royal family. The elder son of Prince George, Duke of Kent, and Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark, he is a grandson of George V, nephew of Edward VIII and George VI, and first cousin of Elizabeth II.

questions.question: Which film-maker, known for blending fairy tales, gothic style and horror, was born on this day in 1964?
questions.explanation: The Mexican director Guillermo del Toro is celebrated for finding beauty in the grotesque.
questions.context:
On this day in 1964: Guillermo del Toro, Mexican-American director, producer, and screenwriter
Guillermo del Toro (Mexican filmmaker (born 1964)): Guillermo del Toro Gómez is a Mexican filmmaker and actor. His work has been characterized by a strong connection to fairy tales, gothicism, and horror, often blending the genres, with an effort to infuse visual or poetic beauty in the grotesque.

questions.question: Which Andrew Lloyd Webber musical opened in London's West End on this day in 1986?
questions.explanation: The Phantom of the Opera premiered in London in 1986 and went on to become the longest-running show on Broadway.
questions.context:

questions.question: On this day in 1676, which Dutch scientist wrote to the Royal Society describing tiny "animalcules"?
questions.explanation: Van Leeuwenhoek, often called the father of microbiology, gave the earliest known account of protozoa.
questions.context:
On this day in 1676: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek wrote a letter to the Royal Society describing "animalcules" – the first known description of protozoa (pictured).
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (Dutch microbiologist (1632–1723)): Antonie Philips van Leeuwenhoek was a Dutch microbiologist and microscopist in the Golden Age of Dutch art, science and technology. A largely self-taught man in science, he is commonly known as "the Father of Microbiology", and one of the first microscopists and microbiologists.

questions.question: Ireland's first public railway opened on this day in 1834, linking Dublin with which harbour?
questions.explanation: The Dublin and Kingstown Railway ran from Westland Row to the harbour at Kingstown, now Dún Laoghaire.
questions.context:
On this day in 1834: Opening of the Dublin and Kingstown Railway, the first public railway on the island of Ireland.
Dublin and Kingstown Railway (Ireland's first passenger railway (1834–1856)): The Dublin and Kingstown Railway (D&KR), which opened in 1834, was Ireland's first passenger railway. It linked Westland Row in Dublin with Kingstown Harbour in County Dublin.
